findings.title: Filtered projection has negative U exponents on an allowed domain element

location.primary: Section 2.2, equation (4) and preceding filtration cutoff

findings.claim: The R-linear projection from the printed filtered part F_i <= s_i is a resolution of the ordinary Alexander-filtered minus complex.

check.input: Sparse 4x4 unknot: linked O cells (0,0),(2,2), free O cells (1,1),(3,3), X cells (0,2),(2,0); diagonal intersection state x. Marking positions are cell centres; state coordinates are vertices.
check.assumptions: One O per row/column, at most one X, free-O condition, q=2, separated X rows and columns including cyclic adjacency, one linked component, integer Alexander lattice, finite monomial satisfies completion boundedness.
check.proof: For the actual a=A_1(x) in Z take s=|a|+1. Then F_1(x)=-a <= s, but P(x)=U_11^(a-|a|-1)x has strictly negative exponent, so it is outside F_2[[U_1,...,U_n]] and the target.
check.counterevidence: Neither nonnegative power-series completion nor sparse-grid restrictions admit the image. Infinity Laurent coefficients are a different theory. No reindexing is stated for the same generator and parameter.
check.local_repair: Changing the cutoff to F_i<=-s_i gives r+a-s-N>=0 for a monomial with r U_11 powers and total N V powers; target Alexander value is s-r<=s. This local proof does not verify the quasi-isomorphism or all downstream conventions.
check.core_dependency: Equation (9) repeats the exponent for I_s^M; for M the whole knot with its induced orientation the same obstruction occurs. Equation (29) composes I into Phi, which enters the surgery differential and Theorems 2.10 and 1.2.
check.limit: This invalidates a printed core construction as stated, not the underlying computability conclusion. Journal status is unverified.

independent_acceptance.source_scope: Checked the sparse-grid definition, free-marking conditions, integer knot Alexander lattice, nonnegative power-series ring, printed filtration and equations(4),(9), the Phi composition and surgery differential.
independent_acceptance.independent_reason: The 4x4 marking pattern has exactly one O per row/column, X only in rows/columns0 and2, and two isolated free O markings. Its linked arcs form one uncrossed rectangle, hence an unknot. For any actual integer Alexander value a the diagonal state x is a legal finite monomial and s=abs(a)+1 gives -a<=s but a-s<=-1. The ring has no inverse U, so the map fails before any analytical Floer result is needed. With cutoff F<=-s, a general monomial U^r V^N x satisfies r+a-s-N>=0 and the image filtration is s-r<=s.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Completion only permits infinite sums of nonnegative powers. The infinity ring is separately defined. The knot orientation equal to the removed whole sublink gives the same exponent in the projection-inclusion map.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency_and_repair: The same invalid map enters equation(29), the surgery differential and Theorems2.10/1.2; retained Major for an undefined core construction. The sign repair proves local well-definedness only and is not a full global quasi-isomorphism repair.

findings.title: Naive totalization of a general hyperbox need not square to zero

location.primary: Section 2.1, equation (1) and ensuing total-complex assertion

findings.claim: The sum of all local hyperbox maps is a differential on the uncompressed total space.

check.input: n=1,d=2,C^0=C^1=C^2=F_2 in internal degree zero; vertex differentials zero; consecutive edge maps identities.
check.assumptions: All required map degrees hold. Relations at displacements zero and one are zero; no displacement-two relation is imposed.
check.proof: In total degrees 0,-1,-2, D e0=e1, D e1=e2, D e2=0, hence D^2 e0=e2 nonzero.
check.counterevidence: For unit hypercubes every possible endpoint displacement is covered by equation (1). Compression produces the two-term identity map in this example and repairs the differential.
check.core_dependency: No use of false uncompressed totalization was established in the core construction. Later descent uses compression, and the surgery indexing is a unit cube.
check.limit: Peripheral overgeneralization; not evidence against the later compressed surgery formula.

independent_acceptance.source_scope: The hyperbox definition allows n1,d1=2 and imposes relations only for displacement0 or1; no global displacement2 relation is stated.
independent_acceptance.independent_reason: With three internal-degree0 copies of F2, zero vertex differentials and identity edges, both required local relations hold. The total grading puts e_j in degree-j; D(e0)=e1, D(e1)=e2, so D^2(e0)=e2. Compression replaces the two edges by their composition in a two-vertex unit cube, and then no nonzero two-step endpoint remains.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Unit cubes satisfy all endpoint relations and later descent explicitly uses compression. The surgery indexing is by sublinks and is a unit cube.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency_and_repair: Retained Minor: no necessary downstream use of the false uncompressed total-complex assertion was established. Restrict that assertion and the induced-total-map assertion to unit cubes or compressed cubes.

findings.title: Unqualified finite-dimensional F_2 quasi-isomorphic replacement cannot preserve completed minus homology

location.primary: First paragraph of page 46 in the proof of Theorem 1.2

findings.claim: The completed minus surgery complex can be replaced by a quasi-isomorphic finite-dimensional complex over F_2.

check.input: The same allowed sparse unknot grid with +1 framing gives S^3 and its unique Spin^c structure.
check.proof: The genus-zero one-generator minus complex has zero differential; after completion its homology is F_2[[U]]. For every N the coefficients of 1,U,...,U^N imply their F_2 linear independence. Thus homology is infinite dimensional. Homology of an m-dimensional complex has dimension at most m, so no finite-total-dimensional complex is quasi-isomorphic.
check.counterevidence: Finite rank/presentation over F_2[[U]], finite grading windows, and degreewise algorithms are possible; they are distinct from the unqualified global finite-dimensional assertion. Discussion of ranks elsewhere suggests an intended restriction but does not supply it.
check.core_dependency: The disputed step is the last finiteness justification in the proof of the principal algorithmic theorem.
check.limit: Computability itself is not refuted. A finite encoding or degreewise repair has not been independently verified. The external truncation proof and the journal version have not been fully checked.

independent_acceptance.source_scope: Theorem1.2 explicitly uses completed minus homology and the definition tensors the usual minus complex with F2[[U]]. The final proof paragraph says quasi-isomorphic finite dimensional complex over F2 without a fixed-degree restriction.
independent_acceptance.independent_reason: Plus-one surgery on the allowed unknot gives S3. In the genus-zero one-generator Heegaard model the differential vanishes, so its completed minus homology contains the linearly independent monomials1,U,...,U^N for everyN. The homology of a finite-total-dimensional F2 complex is finite dimensional, invariant under quasi-isomorphism. Thus the printed global replacement is impossible.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: Finite rank or finite presentation over F2[[U]], fixed-degree truncation and finite algorithmic encoding remain compatible. They are not the stated global finite F2 dimension; surrounding rank language does not insert a restriction into the exact claim.
independent_acceptance.core_dependency_and_repair: Retained Major because the last finiteness justification of the principal algorithm is invalid. Computability itself is not disproved. A proper finite encoding/degreewise truncation with retained tower information would require its own verified argument; no external truncation proof was silently assumed to provide a global finite-dimensional replacement.

scientific_adjudication: Initial version-limited findings; no author acceptance or editorial disposition implied
